title: The Data Coach Chronicles: A systematic review of human support for making data-based decision-making a success
extended_summary:
This paper asks what data coaches do in school-based data-based decision-making (DBDM) initiatives and how those coaches are prepared for their role. The authors frame DBDM as a process in which schools use assessment and other data to inform instructional and school-improvement decisions, and they argue that human support is often essential because teachers and school teams struggle to interpret and act on data effectively.

The study is a systematic review of 20 studies published between 2005 and 2021, drawn from primary and secondary education settings. The included cases involved data coaches or similar support roles in school improvement, professional development, and data-use interventions, mostly in the United States and the Netherlands, with one Canadian case and one New Zealand case. The review synthesizes how data coaches were appointed, what expertise they brought, what tasks they performed, and what professionalization activities supported them.

The main conclusion is that data coaching is highly variable but generally centered on helping school teams analyze, interpret, and act on data. Coaches were often temporary and external, frequently with teaching experience, and their work included data support, analysis, presentation, artifact development, and facilitation of team discussions. Only a minority of studies described explicit professionalization, and the authors conclude that more tailored training, clearer role definitions, and flexible, context-sensitive coaching models are needed to strengthen DBDM in schools.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general generative AI / LLM chatbot used for writing assistance and outlining, rather than a specific named AI product with an educational coaching function.
identified_tools.use_case: The authors disclosed using ChatGPT to assist with outlining the structure of the article, and QuillBot to generate alternative phrasings and help refine language during manuscript preparation. The paper did not study AI for instructional coaching or lesson-plan feedback in schools.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review of human data coaching, not an empirical evaluation of an AI instructional coaching tool. The only AI mention is a writing-assistance disclosure (ChatGPT/QuillBot), which is not part of the study’s research focus or evidence base.
impact_tier_rationale: No educational or school-based AI intervention outcomes were measured. The paper reports no impact of AI on coaching, feedback, learning, or school implementation.
